correctness.rationale: For K<=1 maximum-modulus fixed-point inequality M<=K tanh M rules out all nonzero equilibria. For K>1 the unique positive root r=K tanh r satisfies K sech²r<1. Necessity: if all neighbors have the opposite sign at a nonzero equilibrium, weighted tanh neighbors cannot equal the vertex value at any beta. For a supported binary sign vector, at x=r sigma same-sign weights dominate opposite-sign weights by q0^beta with q0=delta/(2r+delta)<1. On a shrinking q^beta supnorm ball, the full normalized-weight map has Lip bound tending to K sech²r<1 despite equal-opinion absolute-value kinks; its center defect is O(q0^beta). Contraction gives a unique nearby exponentially attracting equilibrium with O(q0^beta) supnorm error for sufficiently large beta. A mixed supported coloring exists exactly if both monochromatic sign classes contain an edge; equivalently graph has two vertex-disjoint edges. Conversely color outward from endpoints of such edges along a rooted spanning forest; the four-vertex path is minimal. Independently enumerated all connected labeled graphs through five vertices and compared supported mixed colorings against matching >=2, obtaining n=2:(1,0),3:(4,0),4:(38,34),5:(728,723).
residual_risks: Does not classify zero-coordinate, multilevel, or all finite-beta equilibria, global attractors, stochastic dynamics; small-graph exhaustive census is only a diagnostic.

The matching proof is graph elementary but the uniform finite-beta fixed-point contraction is the substantive new result. Qualified priority risk remains.

value.rationale: For an established nonlinear social-influence model this proves a sharp, topology-only threshold for the existence of genuine stable polarization: two disjoint edges, witnessed minimally by P4. It also classifies each admissible binary sign pattern and quantifies exponential approach to saturated magnitudes, turning qualitative simulations into a verifiable arbitrary-finite-network theorem.
residual_risks: The result requires large but graph-dependent finite beta and fixed delta>0; it gives no global basin or finite-beta bifurcation classification.

limitations: Does not classify zero-coordinate, multilevel, or all finite-beta equilibria, global attractors, stochastic dynamics; small-graph exhaustive census is only a diagnostic.
